newsitem.title: FRANCE: French consumer spending falls, cars jump in Sept.
newsitem.headline: French consumer spending falls, cars jump in Sept.

text.p: French consumer spending on manufactured goods fell in September despite a sharp rise in car sales as people rushed to beat the end of a new-cars-for-old rebate scheme.
Consumer consumption of manufactured goods fell 1.5 percent during the month while spending on cars rose 18.8 percent. Retail sector spending, which excludes cars, dropped 5.6 percent.
The rise in car sales was overcome by drops in spending on household equipment, textile and leather and other goods, national statistics institute INSEE said.
Many economists had expected spending to rise.

Consumption has been hit by record unemployment of 12.6 percent, which is toughening the task for the already unpopular government as it struggles to reverse a deep sense of economic disappointment in France.
